restoration_note: The teaching describes the four elements (the Living Soul / Five Sons of the First Man) bound to the Cross of Light in the body, where they cast off a graded cascade of "defiled garments" (bond → wrath → desire → bitterness → heat → flesh → gloom → severity, summed as twelve strippings), with two endings: ascent through the New Man's living icon to first rest, or metensomatosis under sentence. The address-formula at {0} ("the chosen one"), the cosmogonic verb ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ at {2}, ⲧⲥⲉⲧ(ⲉ) at {5} (fire as stripping agent), and the chain term ⲟⲩⲥⲛⲁϩ "bond" at {6} are tightly constrained by the apparatus and the spiritual arc; routine grammatical fills ({3} ⲉⲩ-, {7}–{10} word continuations, {19} ⲉⲧ-, {20} ⲍⲛ̄, {22} ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ ⲁ-, {26} ⲅ) follow standard Coptic morphology. The large lacunae at {16}–{17} (15–16 chars), the ambiguous numeric phrase at {12}–{15} (where the Coptic ϣⲙ̄ⲛⲧ does not match the English "eight" cleanly), the partially traced {11} and {21}, and the verb-fragments at {23}–{25} are too damaged or weakly constrained to restore responsibly. {1} (4 chars after ⲉⲓⲙⲉ) and {4} (4 chars in "ⲍⲛ̄ ⲟⲩ ⲛ-...") admit several plausible fills but no decisive constraint.

restorations.basis: Editor's restoration completes ⲡⲉⲧⲥⲁⲧϥ̄ 'the chosen one,' the customary vocative addressing the disciple in Kephalaia openings; qualitative substantive of ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ matches the regenerate frame.
Only one trace (ⲧ) and ~4 chars; the object of ⲉⲓⲙⲉ 'knew' could be ϫⲉ-clause, demonstrative, or pronominal — no decisive constraint.
Lexicon entry 'Mingling' = ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ̄ — exactly the cosmogonic verb for Error/Darkness's first-contest mingling with Light; aligns with the spiritual reading's account of the primal war.
Circumstantial 3pl prefix ⲉⲩ- before ⲕⲁ-ⲕⲟⲩ 'leave them'; required by the syntax of the temporal clause.
4-char gap after ⲟⲩ ⲛ-: candidates include ⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'sin,' ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ 'error,' or a likeness/form term, none decisively constrained by trace or context.
ⲧⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'the fire' (lexicon: Fire / love-as-purifying agent) — feminine subject of ϣⲁⲣⲉ; the visible ⲉ is the final letter of ⲧⲥⲉⲧⲉ. The fire is the stripping agent in the elements' purification.
Restores ⲟ[ⲩⲥⲛ]ⲁϩ 'a bond' (lexicon: bond = ⲥⲛⲁϩ/ⲙ̄ⲣⲣⲉ); confirmed by line 18's ⲡⲃⲱϣ ⲙ̄ⲡⲥⲛⲁϩ 'the nakedness of the bond,' which presupposes 'bond' as the immediately preceding term.
Completes ⲡⲍⲙⲁⲙ 'the heat' (Lyc. ⲍⲙⲁⲙ = Sah. ϩⲙⲟⲙ), continuing ⲡⲍ- at end of preceding line; required by the cascade chain bitterness → heat.
Completes ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ 'of them' (3pl object), continuing ⲙ̄- at end of previous line; standard pronominal object suffix.
Definite article ⲡ- before ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ; the formula ⲡⲕⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲏⲩ ⲙ̄... 'the stripping naked of...' is repeated throughout the cascade.
Completes ⲁⲍⲏⲩ 'naked' continuing from ⲛ̄ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁ- at end of previous line; fixed formula.
Partial trace 'ⲛ̄ⲍⲣ . ⲟⲩ' over 5 chars suggests a noun like ϩⲣⲏⲣⲉ 'flower' or related plural, but no fixed parallel constrains the construct 'the [N] of the winds of shame.'

4-char gap before ϣⲙ̄ⲛⲧ; likely 'ⲡⲉ ⲡⲓ-' or similar copular phrase, but the numeric term itself (three vs. eight — the English 'eight' does not match Coptic ϣⲙ̄ⲛⲧ which is closer to 'three') is unstable, undermining the whole clause structure.
4-char gap after ϣⲙ̄ⲛⲧ; the noun governed by the numeral is unconstrained — could be ⲱⲏⲛ 'trees,' a faculty term, or a structural unit.
Editor's tentative ⲙⲓⲏ is itself marked uncertain ('[?]'); no parallel formula or clear semantic anchor in the spiritual reading to confirm it. Honest non-restoration preferred.
Partial 'ⲡⲥⲉ' + 4 chars allows ⲡⲥⲉⲡⲓ 'remainder,' ⲡⲥⲉⲡ 'occasion,' or other ⲥⲉ- nouns; no decisive constraint for 'the [X] of the twelve strippings.'
16-char gap at start of clause about the four elements; size is too large and context too thin for a constrained restoration.
15-char gap leading into 'that which they gather inward'; no formula or trace to anchor a fill.
Single-character editor restoration giving ⲟⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩ 'they bring them' (Lyc. ⲟⲛ̄ⲧ⸗, construct of ⲉⲓⲛⲉ); habitual sense fits the iterative description of the elements' work in the body's economy.
Relative marker ⲉⲧ- introducing the antecedent confirmed by parallel ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲛⲏⲩ later in the same line.
Restores ⲍⲛ̄ 'in' (Lyc. for ϩⲛ̄); standard locative governing 'their living icon.'
Partial ϩ + 4 chars after ϣⲁⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄ 'they live'; numerous possible adverbial extensions (ⲁⲡⲉϩ, ⲡⲱϩ, ⲣⲏϩ etc.) without decisive constraint.
Standard Manichaean idiom ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ ⲁ- 'upward to'; lexicon 'ascend' = ⲃⲱⲕ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈; only the inflected ending and preposition need restoration.

8-char gap matching ⲁⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ 'into the body'; the parallel earlier in the teaching (ⲡⲥⲁⲡ ⲇⲉ ⲉⲧⲁⲩⲛⲏⲩ ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲡⲥⲱⲙⲁ, line 9) and the spiritual reading's contrast — 'when the elements come into the body of sinners, defilements multiply' — strongly support this fill.
1-char gap completing a verb beginning ⲧⲛ-; possible candidates (ⲧⲛϯ, ⲧⲛⲁⲩ, ⲧⲛϩⲟ) too varied to fix.
Partial ⲥⲟ + 3 chars; many ⲥⲟ- verbs/nouns (ⲥⲟⲡⲥⲡ, ⲥⲟⲩⲧⲱⲛ, ⲥⲟⲡ) possible without context anchor.
Single letter ⲅ completing μετάγγισμός / ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲅⲅⲓⲥⲙⲟⲥ 'transmigration' (lexicon: metensomatosis), continuing from ⲙⲉⲧⲁⲅ at end of previous line; the second ending of the teaching's two-destinies arc.
